## Addendum: Analysis of Bilaterally Pooled OPA Pathway

*Jul 17, 2026*

The GLM effect sizes of bilateral areas along the hypothetical pathway, *V1d $\to$ V2d $\to$ OPA* were pooled. Same analysis was performed on this bilaterally pooled data.

### Structure of RDMs

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-rdm-heatmaps-pooled
#| fig-cap: "**Bilaterally pooled RDM** for participant 26: *Walking direction forms the large blocks, map forms the small blocks within. Brackets show number of voxels in each area*"

# Pool left and right hemisphere voxels/masks per region along the dorsal pathway
pathway_regions = ['v1d', 'v2d', 'opa']
pooled_roi_masks = {}
for region in pathway_regions:
    pooled_mask = None
    for hemi in ['lh', 'rh']:
        native_mask_path = label_dir / f"{hemi}.{region}.top800.nii.gz"
        native_mask_ants = ants.image_read(str(native_mask_path))
        # Transform to MNI space
        transformed_ants = ants.apply_transforms(fixed=ants.from_nibabel_nifti(subject_mask), moving=native_mask_ants,
                                           transformlist=[str(t1w_to_mni_xfm)],
                                           interpolator='genericLabel')
        roi_mask = ants.to_nibabel_nifti(transformed_ants).get_fdata().astype(bool)
        # Pool the two hemispheres together
        pooled_mask = roi_mask if pooled_mask is None else (pooled_mask | roi_mask)
    pooled_roi_masks[region] = pooled_mask & brain_mask_data

# Pull out actual effect sizes per pooled ROI, voxels x (condition x run) observations
betas_4d_data = betas_4d.get_fdata()
pooled_roi_betas_data = {}
for name, mask in pooled_roi_masks.items():
    pooled_roi_betas_data[name] = betas_4d_data[mask]
# Pooled ROI-masked residuals per run, needed for the crossnobis noise precision matrix
pooled_roi_residual_data = {}
for name, mask in pooled_roi_masks.items():
    pooled_roi_residual_data[name] = [res.get_fdata()[mask] for res in run_residuals]

# MAD-based outlier voxel exclusion modified z > 3.5
# Applied to every pooled ROI to exclude any outliers driving statistical analysis
for name in pooled_roi_betas_data:
    voxel_std = pooled_roi_betas_data[name].std(axis=1)
    mad = np.median(np.abs(voxel_std - np.median(voxel_std)))
    modified_z = 0.6745 * (voxel_std - np.median(voxel_std)) / mad
    keep_voxels = np.abs(modified_z) <= 3.5
    pooled_roi_betas_data[name] = pooled_roi_betas_data[name][keep_voxels]
    pooled_roi_residual_data[name] = [res[keep_voxels] for res in pooled_roi_residual_data[name]]

# Neural RSA via rsatoolbox, crossnobis distance
pooled_condition_rdm_objects = {}
for name, roi_data in pooled_roi_betas_data.items():
    # Define the dataset for rsatoolbox
    dataset = rsatoolbox.data.Dataset(
        measurements=roi_data.T,
        obs_descriptors={'map': beta_meta['map'].values,
                          'walking_direction': beta_meta['walking_direction'].values,
                          'map_direction': beta_meta['map_direction'].values,
                          'run': beta_meta['run'].astype(str).values}
    )
    # Compute the noise precision matrix for crossnobis distance
    noise_precision = [rsatoolbox.data.prec_from_residuals(residuals.T)
                        for residuals in pooled_roi_residual_data[name]]
    # Store the raw RDMs object directly, no DataFrame conversion
    pooled_condition_rdm_objects[name] = rsatoolbox.rdm.calc_rdm_crossnobis(dataset, descriptor='map_direction',
                                                                             noise=noise_precision, cv_descriptor='run')

# Final per-pooled-ROI voxel count
pooled_roi_voxel_counts = {name: roi_data.shape[0] for name, roi_data in pooled_roi_betas_data.items()}

# Display the pooled 12x12 map x direction ROI RDMs for the dorsal pathway only
# Walking direction forms the big blocks, map forms the small blocks within each
pooled_region_titles = {'v1d': 'V1d', 'v2d': 'V2d', 'opa': 'OPA'}

# One shared color scale based on off-diagonal values across the pathway
pooled_off_diagonal = []
for region in pathway_regions:
    matrix = pooled_condition_rdm_objects[region].get_matrices()[0]
    pooled_off_diagonal.append(matrix[~np.eye(matrix.shape[0], dtype=bool)])
pooled_off_diagonal = np.concatenate(pooled_off_diagonal)
# 98th percentile of the off-diagonal entries to avoid outlier influence on the color scale
vmax = np.percentile(pooled_off_diagonal, 98)

# Plot the heatmaps
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(pathway_regions), figsize=(4 * len(pathway_regions) + 1, 5),
                          constrained_layout=True,
                          gridspec_kw={'wspace': 0.15})
for col, region in enumerate(pathway_regions):
    rdm_obj = pooled_condition_rdm_objects[region]
    rdm_df = pd.DataFrame(rdm_obj.get_matrices()[0],
                           index=rdm_obj.pattern_descriptors['map_direction'],
                           columns=rdm_obj.pattern_descriptors['map_direction'])
    reordered_rdm = rdm_df.loc[direction_major_order, direction_major_order]
    # Plot the heatmap
    sns.heatmap(reordered_rdm, ax=axes[col], cmap='viridis', vmin=0, vmax=vmax,
                cbar=False, square=True) # Negative values collapsed to zero since they usually represent noise
    axes[col].set_title(f'{pooled_region_titles[region]} ({pooled_roi_voxel_counts[region]})', fontsize=26)
    axes[col].set_xticks([])
    axes[col].set_yticks([])
    # Mark the boundaries between the 4 walking-direction blocks
    for boundary in range(3, 12, 3):
        axes[col].axhline(boundary, color='black', linewidth=1)
        axes[col].axvline(boundary, color='black', linewidth=1)
# One shared vertical colorbar
mappable = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap='viridis', norm=plt.Normalize(vmin=0, vmax=vmax))
cbar = fig.colorbar(mappable, ax=axes[:], orientation='vertical', fraction=0.07, pad=0.02, ticks=[0, vmax])
cbar.ax.set_yticklabels(['0.000', f'{vmax:.3f}'], fontsize=18)
fig.text(1.02, 0.5, 'Crossnobis distance', fontsize=22, rotation=90, va='center', ha='center')
plt.show();
```

*OPA* shows a distinct structure separating directions 1 & 2 from 3 & 4. Directions 1 & 2 have two characters in the back corners of the square and one character in either of the front corners. Directions 3 & 4 have two characters in the front corners and one character in the either of the back corners of the square. Thus the split representational structure is not capturing the laterality of the visual field. The structure maybe representing the overall layout itself. Bilaterally pooled *V1d* and *V2d* show a simialar structure as their left counterparts but the dissimilarity is more pronounced.

### Multidimensional Scaling Visualization

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-pathway-mds-pooled
#| fig-cap: "**Areawise-MDS representational maps along the bilaterally pooled pathway**: *Top row colored by walking direction, bottom row colored by map (position of the characters). Each column is Procrustes-aligned to the previous ROI's MDS for comparison. Stress and participation ratio (PR) % shown per ROI.*"

# Get the number of conditions
n_conditions = len(pooled_condition_rdm_objects[pathway_regions[0]].pattern_descriptors['map_direction'])
# Build the centering matrix
centering_matrix = np.eye(n_conditions) - np.ones((n_conditions, n_conditions)) / n_conditions

pooled_participation_ratios = {}
for name in pathway_regions:
    # Extract the 12x12 squared crossnobis distance matrix
    D = pooled_condition_rdm_objects[name].get_matrices()[0]
    # Compute the similarity matrix
    S = -0.5 * centering_matrix @ D @ centering_matrix
    # Get the eigenvalues of the similarity matrix
    eigenvalues = np.linalg.eigvalsh(S)
    # Clip tiny negative eigenvalues (floating-point noise) to zero
    eigenvalues = np.maximum(eigenvalues, 0)
    # Compute the raw participation ratio
    pr = (eigenvalues.sum() ** 2) / (eigenvalues ** 2).sum()
    # Normalize by the max achievable rank (n - 1, centering removes one dimension)
    pooled_participation_ratios[name] = pr / (n_conditions - 1)

# Peform prodcrustus aligned MDS scaling of RDMs
mds_rows = []
pathway_reference = None
for stage, name in enumerate(pathway_regions):
    rdm_matrix = pooled_condition_rdm_objects[name].get_matrices()[0]
    condition_labels = pooled_condition_rdm_objects[name].pattern_descriptors['map_direction']
    # Scale the RDM down to 2 dimensions
    mds_estimator = MDS(n_components=2, dissimilarity='precomputed', random_state=23, normalized_stress=True, n_init=4)
    mds_coords = mds_estimator.fit_transform(rdm_matrix)
    # Align every ROI's MDS solution to the previous ROI along the pathway, for visualization only
    if stage == 0:
        pathway_reference = mds_coords
    else:
        # Compute the procrustes alignment
        mds_coords = procrustes(pathway_reference, mds_coords)[1]
        # Grab the current ROI's aligned coordinates to use for next ROI's alignment
        pathway_reference = mds_coords
    # Build a tidy row per condition
    for i, label in enumerate(condition_labels):
        mds_rows.append({
            'roi': name,
            'x': mds_coords[i, 0],
            'y': mds_coords[i, 1],
            'direction': label.split('_')[1],
            'map': label.split('_')[0],
            'stress': mds_estimator.stress_,
        })
mds_df = pd.DataFrame(mds_rows)

# Top row: colored by direction, Bottom row: colored by map
direction_palette = sns.color_palette('colorblind', n_colors=4)
map_palette = [sns.color_palette('colorblind')[i] for i in (0, 2, 3)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, len(pathway_regions), figsize=(5 * len(pathway_regions), 10), constrained_layout=True)
for col, name in enumerate(pathway_regions):
    stage_data = mds_df.query('roi == @name')
    pr_pct = pooled_participation_ratios[name] * 100
    title = f'{pooled_region_titles[name]}\nStress: {stage_data["stress"].iloc[0]:.2f} (PR: {pr_pct:.1f}%)'

    # Top row: direction, circles
    sns.scatterplot(stage_data, x='x', y='y', hue='direction', marker='o',
                     palette=direction_palette, s=140, ax=axes[0, col],
                     legend=(col == len(pathway_regions) - 1))
    axes[0, col].set_title(title, fontsize=16)

    # Bottom row: map, squares
    sns.scatterplot(stage_data, x='x', y='y', hue='map', marker='s',
                     palette=map_palette, s=140, ax=axes[1, col],
                     legend=(col == len(pathway_regions) - 1))

    for ax in (axes[0, col], axes[1, col]):
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
        ax.set_xlabel('')
        ax.set_ylabel('')
# Draw each row's legend outside the figure to the right
direction_handles, direction_labels = axes[0, -1].get_legend_handles_labels()
axes[0, -1].get_legend().remove()
map_handles, map_labels = axes[1, -1].get_legend_handles_labels()
axes[1, -1].get_legend().remove()
fig.legend(direction_handles, direction_labels, loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.75), fontsize=16, title='Direction', title_fontsize=16)
fig.legend(map_handles, map_labels, loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.25), fontsize=16, title='Map', title_fontsize=16)
plt.show();
```

All three areas' representational structure separates the walking direction condition much more cleanly as compared to @fig-pathway-mds. *V1d* and *V2d* show directions in the following order: 2, 1, 4, and 3 from top left to to bottom right. *OPA* is separates directions 1 & 2 from direction 4 from top left to bottom right with direction 3 scattered in between. For the map conditions, none of the areas cleanly separate except for *OPA* which separates maps 1 & 2, but map 3's 4 instances are split on two sides. The monotonic increase in PR% is still present between primary visual areas and OPA, but MDS stress is almost equal for all areas. This makes sense since laterality of visual field sensitivities of primary visual areas is well-documented.

### Validation

Multiple regression RSA (MR-RSA)[@Bosch_2025] was performed to control for low-level features using bilaterally pooled *V1d* and *V2d* RDMs. This allowed me to determine whether direction and map categorical RDMs explain unique variance in bilaterally pooled *OPA* RDM. The variance inflation factor (VIF) for the predictors of each model were as follows:

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-mr-rsa-pooled
#| fig-cap: "**MR-RSA model comparison**: *Mean Cosine Similarity with bilaterally pooled OPA RDM, low-level vs hierarchical models. VIF per predictor shown alongside for each model.*"

# Fixed condition order for every model/neural RDM
condition_order = list(pooled_condition_rdm_objects['v1d'].pattern_descriptors['map_direction'])

# Build the 12x12 direction and map model RDMs with directions as primary and map as secondary
directions_12 = [label.split('_')[1] for label in condition_order]
maps_12 = [label.split('_')[0] for label in condition_order]
direction_rdm_12 = (np.array(directions_12)[:, None] != np.array(directions_12)[None, :]).astype(int)
map_rdm_12 = (np.array(maps_12)[:, None] != np.array(maps_12)[None, :]).astype(int)
direction_vec = direction_rdm_12[np.triu_indices(len(condition_order), k=1)]
map_vec = map_rdm_12[np.triu_indices(len(condition_order), k=1)]

# Vectorize the pooled V1d and V2d RDMs
v1d_vec = pooled_condition_rdm_objects['v1d'].get_vectors()[0]
v2d_vec = pooled_condition_rdm_objects['v2d'].get_vectors()[0]

# VIF for each predictor to look for collinearity of factors, computed separately per model
def compute_vif(predictor_dict):
    predictors = pd.DataFrame(predictor_dict)
    # Add the intercept column
    predictors_with_const = predictors.assign(const=1.0)
    return pd.Series(
        [variance_inflation_factor(predictors_with_const.values, i)
         for i in range(predictors.shape[1])],
        index=predictors.columns, name='VIF')

vif_low_level = compute_vif({'V1d': v1d_vec, 'V2d': v2d_vec})
vif_direction = compute_vif({'V1d': v1d_vec, 'V2d': v2d_vec, 'Direction': direction_vec})
vif_direction_map = compute_vif({'V1d': v1d_vec, 'V2d': v2d_vec, 'Direction': direction_vec, 'Map': map_vec})

# Build the baseline model with only primary visual RDMs
low_level_model = rsatoolbox.model.ModelWeighted('low_level', np.vstack([v1d_vec, v2d_vec]))

# Build the first hierarchical model, direction only
direction_model = rsatoolbox.model.ModelWeighted('low_level_direction', np.vstack([v1d_vec, v2d_vec, direction_vec]))

# Build the second hierarchical model, direction and map
direction_map_model = rsatoolbox.model.ModelWeighted('low_level_direction_map',
                                                       np.vstack([v1d_vec, v2d_vec, direction_vec, map_vec]))

# Compare the three models using bootstrap
# Suppress eval_bootstrap_pattern's hardcoded tqdm progress bar, which writes to stderr
with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
    results = rsatoolbox.inference.eval_bootstrap_pattern(
        models = [low_level_model, direction_model, direction_map_model],
        data = pooled_condition_rdm_objects['opa'],
        N = 1000
    )

# Store the result into a tidy DataFrame
model_labels = ['Low-Level Model\n(V1d + V2d)', 'Hierarchical Model 1\n(+ Direction)', 'Hierarchical Model 2\n(+ Direction + Map)']
bootstrap_df = pd.DataFrame(results.evaluations, columns=model_labels).melt(var_name='Model', value_name='Cosine Similarity')

# Compute the 2.5th/97.5th percentile of the bootstrap distribution
def percentile_ci_95(x):
    return np.percentile(x, 2.5), np.percentile(x, 97.5)

# Plot the mean cosine similarity per model with 95% CI error bars, alongside a VIF table per model
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5.5))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(1, 2, width_ratios=[1.3, 1], wspace=0.20)
ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0])
sns.pointplot(data=bootstrap_df, x='Model', y='Cosine Similarity', hue='Model', palette='colorblind',
              legend=False, errorbar=percentile_ci_95, capsize=0.2, linestyle='none', ax=ax)
for i, mean in enumerate(results.get_means()):
    ax.text(i + 0.05, mean, f'{mean:.3f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Mean Cosine Similarity to OPA RDM')
ax.set_ylim([0, 1])
ax.set_xlabel('')
ax.set_title('MR-RSA: Dorsal Pathway (no laterality)')

# VIF table alongside the model comparison plot
ax_table = fig.add_subplot(gs[1])
ax_table.axis('off')
vif_combined = pd.DataFrame({
    'Low-Level\nModel': vif_low_level.reindex(['V1d', 'V2d', 'Direction', 'Map']),
    'Hierarchical\nModel 1': vif_direction.reindex(['V1d', 'V2d', 'Direction', 'Map']),
    'Hierarchical\nModel 2': vif_direction_map.reindex(['V1d', 'V2d', 'Direction', 'Map']),
}).round(2)
cell_text = vif_combined.fillna('—').values
tbl = ax_table.table(cellText=cell_text, colLabels=vif_combined.columns, rowLabels=vif_combined.index,
                      loc='center', cellLoc='center', colWidths=[0.25, 0.25, 0.25])
tbl.auto_set_font_size(False)
tbl.set_fontsize(9)
tbl.scale(1, 2.2)
ax_table.set_title('VIF per model', fontsize=12, pad=10)
plt.show();
```

@fig-mr-rsa-pooled shows that hierarchical models are more similar to left OPA RDM than the low-level model, but the 95% confidence intervals overlap for all three models. Thus pooling of bilateral areas leads to the same conclusion reached with the left pathway.
